analysis.title: Europe Open - Full house of catalysts
key_insights: RBNZ surprised with a hold at 2.75% vs consensus of a 25bp hike. The vote was 4-3 and all members agreed tighter policy is likely needed, so the split reflects timing. Citi's house view is now a hike in Dec. NZDUSD fell 1.2% on volume 4.5x recent averages, with 0.5600 holding as support.
OIS still prices a hefty NZ tightening cycle: +21bp for Dec, then 17-18bp per meeting, 92bp cumulative into mid-2027, which Citi says has room to reprice.

Australian Q3 trimmed mean CPI rose 1% QoQ, in line with Citi, supporting Citi's call for a 25bp RBA hike next week. Nov OIS hike pricing rose from 16bp to 21bp, but AUDUSD got no boost. 0.7050 is strong technical resistance.
Citi trader Pat Hu says going long AUD should wait, possibly adding on a move toward 0.6930-50 in AUDUSD and 1.5940-50 in EURAUD. AUDNZD hit new highs above 1.25.
US 10-year yield is at 5.02% on higher oil prices. The Citi desk saw better selling in intermediates and interest in 5s/5s. Citi rates strategists see a case for more global 2s5s flattening momentum.
WSJ reports the US told several Gulf countries to prepare for a short, intense military campaign after the US midterms. No final decision has been made by President Trump. Oil rose on the report.

UK Autumn Budget at 12:30 GMT: Citi expects fiscal headroom of £14-15bn and a market-friendly outcome. Headroom below £10bn would be a negative surprise. Citi sees EURGBP downside and FTSE 100 tactically outperforming the FTSE 250, but wants the FOMC to clear before trading cable.
Gilt remit: Citi strategists expect funding to rise £11bn, with +£5bn via gilts (to £251.2bn) and +£6bn via Treasury bills.

BoC at 13:45 GMT: OIS prices a hike at about 20bp, but Citi economists expect a hold at 2.25%. Bloomberg economists are split 17/35 between hike and hold. A hold would likely carry hawkish guidance. STIRT prefers being paid in the front meeting. USDCAD broke above 1.40 on leveraged CAD short covering.

FOMC at 18:00 GMT: wide consensus for a hold, with 2bp priced and no SEP update. Citi's house view is a final 25bp hike in Dec. The key question is whether Chair Warsh acknowledges tighter financial conditions after the AI-led equity selloff. Citi says any USD weakness should be faded.

SK Hynix Q3 results drove Kospi up 6%. Profit rose to KRW 83.3tn on higher memory ASPs and high-value product sales. The company announced about KRW 100trn more to shareholders, including KRW 14trn Q3 dividends and a 20tn buyback.
Microsoft and Alphabet report after the US close. Straddles are priced at SPX 0.65%, QQQ 1.11% and IWM 1.15%. Tech megacap earnings are a bigger driver for US equities than the FOMC.
SPX FOMC event premium has compressed to 0.67% implied vs 0.66% realized average over the prior 8 meetings. SPX has traded down on 6 FOMC days in a row.

Israel's election is deadlocked, with Netanyahu's bloc and the opposition each tracking toward 51 seats and two Israeli Arab parties expected to win 18. USDILS rose to 3.07 (+0.80%). Citi's local desk calls it market negative, with AI and US equity sentiment a key driver of the shekel.

FX flows: leveraged names bought GBP and AUD and sold USD, JPY and EUR overnight. USD rallied and EURUSD is attempting to break 1.11. Citi stays bearish on EUR but prefers crosses EURGBP, EURCHF and EURAUD.
BoT held rates at 1%, in line with expectations.

Trump said a meeting involving Putin and Zelenskyy would soon be arranged to end the Russia-Ukraine war.
Israel's general election is deadlocked between Netanyahu's bloc and the Eisenkot-led opposition, with Israeli Arab parties potentially decisive.
